Process

Process for Full Assistance Package

Here's exactly what happens, step by step, once you reserve your slot.

Step 1

Reserve your slot

Get your quote and message us to confirm your slot and lock in your booking — this covers your DS-160 preparation, scheduling account setup, biometrics and interview scheduling, document collation, script writing, and one mock interview.

Next opening: Thu, Nov 12, 2026 — 3:00 PM (Manila time) · Reserve now →

Step 2

Share your details

Send us your full name, intended travel date, and payment date and method so we can track your payment and open your file.

Step 3

Complete our intake form

Fill out our Google Form — it asks the same questions you'll see on the official DS-160, so we can prepare your form accurately.

Step 4

DS-160 drafting

Our team completes your DS-160 and sends you a draft to review. If anything's missing, we'll ask you for it.

Step 5

Scheduling account setup

We set up your US visa scheduling account for you — or if you already have one, just send us the username, password, and your 3 security question answers.

Step 6

Strategy call

We go through your completed DS-160 together, positioning your application properly and fixing any red flags.

Step 7

Visa fee payment & scheduling

Pay your US Embassy visa fee (over the counter at RCBC, by your own card, or through us), then give us 3 possible biometrics dates and 3 possible interview dates so we can book what's available.

Step 8

DS-160 submission

After a thorough final review, we submit your DS-160 — always before your biometrics appointment.

Step 9

Script & mock interview

We prepare and send you your script, then hold a full mock interview — playing the consul, asking the questions likely for your case, and giving you feedback plus reminders on what to bring and wear.

Step 10

Interview day and beyond

Complete your biometrics at Parqal Mall, Parañaque, then your interview at the US Embassy on Roxas Boulevard. If approved, we help you track pickup or delivery of your passport.

📌 Good to know: the US Embassy doesn't actually require you to submit any documents. Supporting documents — like a Certificate of Employment, payslips, ITR, or proof of business and income — are recommended to bring to your interview, but they are not required to be submitted. To apply for a US visa, you only need a valid passport.

FAQ

Common questions

What's the difference between New Application and Reapplication pricing?

A reapplication (previously refused) requires additional review of your past application and an assessment of the likely reasons for refusal, so we can rebuild a stronger strategy. New applications are ₱5,290 per applicant; reapplications are ₱5,690 per applicant.

What exactly is included in the assistance fee?

One-on-one consultation, full DS-160 completion, application review, strategy planning for your travel narrative and ties to the Philippines, setup of your US visa scheduling account, help paying the visa fee, biometrics scheduling at Parqal, interview scheduling, and a 1-on-1 mock interview with a script.

Are there costs on top of your fee?

Yes — two costs go directly to other parties, not to Mommy Di: the US visa application fee (US$185, about ₱11,840) paid to the US Embassy, and a ₱750 delivery fee to 2GO once your visa is approved. The assistance fee above covers guidance and service only.

I already filed my own DS-160 — can you still help?

Yes, that's what Coaching Only (₱3,500) is for: a review of your DS-160, flags on anything that needs editing, and mock interview practice. It's built for DIY applicants, not for applicants currently working with a travel agency.

Can you guarantee my visa will be approved?

No one can guarantee a visa outcome — that decision belongs solely to the US Embassy. What this service does is help you avoid common red flags, build an honest and clear narrative, and prepare thoroughly for your interview to give you the strongest possible chance.

What happens right after I book?

Once your payment is in, we start your file: sharing our intake form, drafting your DS-160, and setting up your scheduling account. From there, we hold your one-on-one strategy call so I can personally review your application and help position it in the best way.

What are the requirements I need to prepare?

The US Embassy doesn't actually require you to submit any documents for a tourist visa application — you only need a valid passport to apply. Supporting documents like a Certificate of Employment, payslips, ITR, or proof of business and income aren't required to be submitted; they're just recommended to bring with you to the interview, in case the consul asks to see them.

Where do we process everything — is there a face-to-face meeting?

Everything is processed online with my team, and all your information is kept private and confidential. Our calls are done over WhatsApp, Viber, or Google Meet — there's no face-to-face meeting required.

Visa approval decisions are made solely by the U.S. Embassy. This service provides preparation, strategy, and coaching — it does not guarantee a specific outcome.
